sessionId.locator: thread.started.thread_id, first row of the public JSONL event stream the runner captures from the client

providers.notes: The first vendor with a capture reader (claude_code is the second), stamped runner_enforced by the same derivation. The session id is announced rather than pinned, so the rollout must be searched for under the sessions root and matched to the public thread.started id — codex-rollout.mjs does that walk and rejects anything outside the root. Strongest at driving the dev loop as well. Historical strict-code-mode and direct-MCP receipts remain readable through src/blind/receipt_binding.ts.

sessionId.locator: --session-id <uuid>, appended by the runner at launch. It is NOT in launch.argv because PlaytestLaunchSchema substitutes only {MODEL}, {CWD} and {MCP_CONFIG}; a {SESSION_ID} token would let the flag live here, and until one exists the runner must append the pair itself.

providers.notes: The second vendor the derivation stamps runner_enforced, and the one that proves the seam is a seam rather than a Codex-shaped hole. Stronger to capture than codex: --session-id PINS the id, so the log path is exact BEFORE launch and the reader never has to pick the newest file in a directory and hope no other Claude Code was running. No rootEnv is declared — CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR exists, but this checkout has not verified that it relocates the per-session log, and naming an env var on faith is exactly the lie this file exists to prevent; the pinned id already keeps concurrent cohort members apart under one shared root. The old argv here was decorative and wrong in two ways: --permission-mode plan REFUSES the game's state-mutating tools, so every session would have died on the first step_action, and --add-dir {CWD} handed the player filesystem access it must never have. The replacement is the flag set verified live against claude 2.1.251: --tools "" removes every built-in tool, --strict-mcp-config plus --mcp-config admits only the adventureforge server, --setting-sources "" and --disable-slash-commands drop settings, skills and hooks, and the init event on the stream reports the resulting surface back so blind-tester/claude-session.mjs can audit what was OFFERED, not merely what was called. Permission is granted by ONE explicit allow rule — --allowedTools mcp__adventureforge — and by no --permission-mode flag at all. A player holding no built-in tools needs exactly one thing granted, the game's MCP server, and naming that server is the smallest way to say it; the client reports the resulting mode back on the init event as "default", which claude 2.1.261 accepts as an OBSERVED value but not as a --permission-mode ARGUMENT (its choices are acceptEdits, auto, manual, dontAsk, plan and the blanket bypass), so asking for it explicitly would fail to launch. The blanket permission-bypass mode this entry used to carry was both more privilege than a tool-less player can use and unlaunchable where this lane actually runs: the client refuses that mode outright when the process is root, as every containerized runner here is, so a live cohort died about six seconds in — before one tool call, one game turn, or one line of evidence — on the client's own root/sudo refusal. The allow rule spells the server name out because PlaytestLaunchSchema substitutes only {MODEL}, {CWD} and {MCP_CONFIG} and there is no token for it; blind-tester/run.sh writes that same name into the --mcp-config it hands over, and nothing has pinned the two together since the 2026-09-23 suite halving retired tests/regression/claude_capture_contract.test.ts, so keep them in step by hand: a rename on one side alone would leave the grant covering nothing and every game tool would then be denied silently, mid-wave.

Well suited to cheap mass-parallel volume cohorts. Ships a CLI, but declares no capture block — nothing here can locate or read its session logs — so the registry DERIVES operator_attested and its sessions are hand-played and ingested until a reader module exists.

Grok Build has a headless CLI and a dedicated `npm run playtest:grok-wave` lane. That lane gives each player an isolated pure AdventureForge MCP server and binds the report to server-authored run evidence, but this checkout has no Grok session-log capture reader with which to prove the complete client tool boundary. Sessions therefore remain operator_attested and cannot move experience metrics. Do not add this provider to blind-tester/implemented-launch-paths.json until both a hardened run.sh launch branch and an auditable Grok capture reader exist.

The desktop/web client remains a separate operator-attested source. Sessions are captured by the operator and ingested with `npm run playtest:ingest`; use the distinct grok_cli provider for the repository's headless Grok wave. kind=desktop_client ensures this entry can never be mislabeled runner_enforced.
